instructions: sqzer is a multi-format image optimizer: a Rust workspace with a codec-free core, backends behind feature flags in three licence tiers, a SSIMULACRA2 target search and a CLI. CLAUDE.md is the rule book and docs/adr holds the decisions; review against them. The project never writes its own decoder, encoder, resampler, colour transform or metric; it adapts mature crates. Prefer fewer, well-chosen dependencies over coverage.

rules.rule: No `unsafe` outside the `heif-dl`, `heif-imageio` and `heif-wic` crates. The workspace sets `forbid(unsafe_code)`; a backend that needs it gets its own binding crate with a safe API.

Reject any new dependency on `zenwebp`, `zenjpeg`, `zenavif`, `zenravif`, `zenjxl`, `jxl-encoder`, `rav1d-safe`, `heic`, `jpegli-rs`, `jpegxl-rs` or `jpegxl-sys`, any AGPL crate outside `sqzer-codecs-agpl`, and any loosening of `deny.toml`. A new dependency's licence must be on the `deny.toml` allow-list and stated in the PR.

A missing encoder returns `Error::EncoderUnavailable`; a setting an encoder cannot honour returns `Error::Unsupported`. Flag any code path that quietly picks another format, another encoder or an approximation of what was asked.

`sqzer-core` depends on nothing in the workspace and never on a codec crate, `image` or `zune-image`. `sqzer-codecs` and `sqzer-metrics` depend on `sqzer-core` only; `sqzer` depends on those three; `sqzer-cli` and `sqzer-wasm` depend on `sqzer` only. Flag any reverse edge.

The `portable` feature set must stay pure Rust, permissively licensed and buildable on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. C bindings go behind a `native-*` feature. Nothing in `sqzer-core` spawns threads; `rayon` is compiled out on wasm.

Backend-only knobs go through `codec_specific`, never as new fields on `EncodeParams`. Adding a format or backend must not touch the CLI grammar, presets, the metric loop or the JSON output. Every decoder honours `DecodeOpts::max_pixels` before allocating.

A new backend needs a round-trip test on the fixtures, a test that its `EncoderCaps` are truthful, and for an encoder a golden SSIMULACRA2 score in `crates/sqzer/tests/golden.rs`. `tests/fixtures` stays under 2 MB.

A behaviour change updates `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased in the same PR, as `* **scope:** subject` under `### Features`, `### Bug Fixes` or `### Performance Improvements`, with the crate as the scope.
An accepted ADR is never rewritten; ticking or annotating its own action items is fine. An architecture change gets a new numbered file and a row in `docs/adr/README.md`.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` is generated by `dist generate` from `dist-workspace.toml`; a hand edit to the workflow is wrong. The per-target native set lives in `crates/sqzer-native-tier/Cargo.toml` and `crates/sqzer-cli/src/native_set.rs` and the two change together.
`Cargo.lock` is never edited by hand and a feature PR does not run a blanket `cargo update`; the lock diff should contain only the crates the PR adds or bumps on purpose.

User-facing text (README, rustdoc, CLI help, error messages, changelog): sentence-case headings, backticks on every identifier and flag, no em dashes, no emoji, no tables, explanation in `#` comments above a command rather than prose around it, uncertainty stated flatly with the next step named.
